hypothesis: Scaling the parent's fan-out damping by using a stronger exponent (w=1/(1+log1p(k)) applied as an extra multiplicative factor on top of the existing 1/log1p(k+1)) pushes hub/clock nets further out of the gradient so the cut term concentrates on genuine signal nets, reducing crit_cross and TNS on all circuits without touching the balance term (which the history shows is fragile).
analysis: Hypothesis partly held: crit_cross fell on C1 (0.011→0.005) and C3 (0.069→0.047), with cut/wcut and repair_flips down modestly, consistent with hub nets leaving the gradient. But C3's score collapsed (-0.160, dWNS -29.9%, one seed -0.46) and C2 regressed slightly; TNS barely moved (+0.008). Seed spread is unacceptable (std 0.093, C3 outlier). Next step: gate the extra damping to high-fanout nets only (or cap the exponent) and re-test C3 across more seeds to confirm the outlier is variance, not a real WNS regression.
